uncited: It differs from sibling methods like [Inter-Ray Coherency](1030-inter-ray-coherency.md) by exploiting depth coherence within a single ray's path rather than spatial coherence between adjacent rays, allowing for batched processing of primitives against multiple depth intervals simultaneously.
Create tiles $T$ from image dimensions $w, h$ and bin count $b$.
A technique to partition ray space into discrete depth intervals, allowing batched primitive testing.
It is chosen when depth coherence is high and primitives are sparse.

It differs from pixel-based assignment by grouping rays, enabling coarser culling.
